ledger.claim: This is an upfront-quoted trip, so the remedy is fixed by POL-RD-11 and not by the distance/time reconstruction of POL-RD-02. EV-FARE-00525 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 13.00, and the fare artifact itself states that on such a trip POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is computed. The rider is therefore not asking the tribunal to re-price the drive; she is asking only for the amount by which the sum taken from her exceeded the price she was quoted at booking.

POL-RD-11(a) refunds in full any amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. On this ledger that is 17.50 charged less 13.00 quoted less 0.00 properly chargeable = SGD 4.50, and the fare artifact publishes that same figure as its own pol_rd_11_remedy, with pol_rd_11_remedy_available true. The amount is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and already lands on a 0.05 boundary, so no rounding question arises.

No pass-through or statutory line absorbs any part of that differential, so the whole SGD 4.50 is exposed. erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is 0.00; the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport (Bedok Mall to Parkway Parade) so no airport surcharge is chargeable on these facts; and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. properly_chargeable.total of 0.00 leaves nothing on the rider's side of the ledger to set against the overcharge.

The driver's own filed statement removes any suggestion that the extra SGD 4.50 bought something on this trip. He says he 'keyed in the other passenger's amount by mistake' - an admission that the sum charged was not the price the rider agreed to and was not consideration for this drive. Read against the ledger, the differential is a keying error measured against the SGD 13.00 upfront quote, and POL-RD-11(a) returns it in full.

The rider does not need a route-deviation finding and does not pretend to one. EV-GPS-00525 records trace_distance_km 4.58 against an optimal 4.4 km - an excess of 0.18 km and 4.09% - which fails both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate (0.8 km absolute and 20%), and the derived block states the status as 'no deviation'. That is precisely why the overcharge cannot be dressed up as a distance charge: the trace distance and the billed 4.6 km agree, so the SGD 4.50 is not explained by the road at all but by the amount keyed. POL-RD-11(a) is available whether or not a deviation is established, and the rider's case rests there.

ledger.claim: The driver's own device trace measures this trip at 4.58 km against an optimal route of 4.4 km — an excess of just 0.18 km, or 4.09% (ev-gps-00525.derived.deviation). POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed 0.8 km AND exceed 20% of the optimal distance; both tests must pass, and this trace fails both by a wide margin. No route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. The rounded 4.5% deviation_pct carried on the trip record is not the governing figure — POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, and the trace figure is 4.09%.

POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider: she must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired — 85 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s, admissibility weight 1.0 — and it shows an excess of 0.18 km / 4.09%, below both POL-RD-01 gates. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the deviation claim is not sustained.

POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either establishment test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's grievance — that the driver 'entered the wrong amount' — is a fare-keying complaint dressed up as a route deviation. On the question actually put by this dispute the trace answers in the driver's favour, and the route-deviation limb of the case is NO_ACTION.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and the quoted fare was SGD 13.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. The rider is already whole on distance and time, and the excess here is only 4.09% in any event.

The rider contests the full SGD 17.50, and nothing in the policy supports that. On an upfront-quoted fare the platform's own fare model publishes the only figure the record could yield — the SGD 4.50 difference between the 13.00 quoted and the 17.50 charged (pol_rd_11_remedy) — and no clause supports a FULL_REFUND here. The driver's statement on file explains the discrepancy candidly as a back-to-back booking keyed against the wrong passenger, a clerical slip, not a route choice and not any conduct the policy penalises.

POL-RD-09's billing-integrity route is empty on this record. The fare carries no ERP gantry lines (erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00), and the trip does not originate at an airport — pickup is Bedok Mall, not Changi or Seletar. There is no unmatched gantry or wrongly applied surcharge for POL-RD-09(4) to bite on, so no billing-integrity finding can be recorded against the driver.

The driver shows zero deviation flags in the last 90 days against 250 completed trips — a ratio of 0.00, below both the 3-flag limb and the 0.05-with-40-trips limb of POL-RD-06. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is available. The rider's request for anything beyond a minor correction therefore has no footing in the policy.

The rider's assertion that this is 'the fourth time in a year' comes with no evidence ID for any of the three alleged earlier incidents; POL-RD-08 provides that an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. Her own profile records no substantiated route-deviation claim in the last 60 days, and POL-GEN-01 forbids any adverse finding built on profile history rather than this trip's own evidence.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the money moves, but only the amount that was charged above the quoted price. The fare you paid was SGD 17.50 (EV-FARE-00525, charged_total) against the SGD 13.00 quoted at booking (EV-FARE-00525, quoted_fare_sgd). This was an upfront-quoted trip (EV-FARE-00525, fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE), so the distance and time charges were fixed when the ride was booked and POL-RD-11 governs; POL-RD-02 does not run. POL-RD-11(a) refunds in full whatever was charged above that fixed quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Nothing is properly chargeable here: the ERP lines are 0.00, the trip ran from Bedok Mall to Parkway Parade and so neither originated nor ended at an airport, so no airport surcharge applies, and the waiting-time fee was 0.00 (properly_chargeable.total 0.00). The whole differential is therefore returned: 17.50 less 13.00 less 0.00 = SGD 4.50, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and already lands on a 0.05 boundary. The driver's statement that he keyed the other passenger's amount by mistake explains how the figure arose and is consistent with the ledger; it does not defeat the refund, because the rider agreed to SGD 13.00 and the extra SGD 4.50 was not the price of this drive. On the route-deviation limb the driver is correct: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00525) measures 4.58 km against an optimal 4.4 km, an excess of 0.18 km / 4.09%, and POL-RD-01 requires an excess both above 0.8 km and above 20%. Both gates fail, so no deviation exists and no distance refund arises; the trace is unimpaired (85 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps), so the rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is not met on the road and never shifts to the driver. So the driver's claim of NO_ACTION is right about the route and wrong about the fare. No repeat-deviation pattern is established: the driver profile shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 250 completed trips, below both limbs of POL-RD-06, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. The rider's assertion that this is the fourth such incident in a year cites no evidence ID for the earlier occasions and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; profile history is context only under POL-GEN-01. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00525-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is not relied on by either party and does not affect this ruling. The deciding figure is carried by EV-FARE-00525 at weight 1.0, so no discount applies.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
